name: FilmCraft
tagline: A free, open-source video editor that works like Premiere Pro - timeline editing, color grading and export, on your own machine.
sentence: Cut clips on a multi-track timeline, grade the color with scopes and curves, and export a finished video - without paying Adobe $23 a month for Premiere.
replaces: Adobe Premiere Pro ($23/month Creative Cloud subscription)

visual.alt: FilmCraft editing Apollo 11 launch footage: a multi-track timeline with titles, b-roll, picture and audio tracks, a Lumetri Color panel with color wheels, and the launch at Complex 39A in the preview.
visual.caption: The editor with Apollo 11 footage, showing the timeline, Lumetri-style color grading and the preview monitor.

board.say: You need to cut a video - trim clips, add transitions, grade the color, export an MP4 - but Premiere costs $23 a month and the free alternatives feel limited.
board.eg: You have 20 minutes of footage and need a polished 3-minute video with titles, transitions and color correction.

board.say: You open FilmCraft and import your footage, or point an AI agent at it through its command interface.
board.eg: Import your video files and start cutting - the timeline uses the same three-point editing and trim tools Premiere users know.

board.say: Your video and audio files: H.264, HEVC, ProRes, VP9, AV1, DNxHD and more - decoded by FilmCraft's own codecs, not a third-party library.
board.eg: Drop in MP4 files from your phone, ProRes files from a camera, or MXF files from a broadcast workflow.

board.say: It gives you a full editing workspace with a multi-track timeline, color grading, effects and titling.
steps: Cut and arrange clips on a multi-track timeline with three-point editing, ripple/roll/slip/slide trims, and J/K/L playback
Grade the color with a Lumetri-style panel: color wheels, curves, HSL secondaries and scopes
Add from about 55 video effects and 30 transitions, with keyframes and Bezier interpolation
Export as H.264 MP4, ProRes, MXF or image sequences - with broadcast-standard loudness metering
board.eg: The README demo: import footage, add a title track, grade with color wheels, and export an H.264 MP4.

board.say: A finished video file, exported on your own computer.

outputs.eg: An H.264 MP4 ready to upload, or a ProRes file for further editing
SRT, WebVTT or broadcast caption formats (SCC, CEA-608/708), exported alongside the video
Export as Final Cut Pro XML, OpenTimelineIO, EDL or AAF to move between editors

before: Cutting a video with color grading and proper export means paying Adobe $23 a month - or using a free editor with fewer codec and format options.
Moving a project between editors means hoping the interchange format works. Many free editors don't support broadcast formats.
after: A full timeline editor with Premiere-style color grading, on your machine, for free - including its own H.264, HEVC and ProRes codecs.
Export your project as Final Cut Pro XML, OpenTimelineIO or EDL and move it to another editor if you outgrow this one.
uses_note: FilmCraft is 9 days old and about 50-60% ready for real work by its own estimate. Named use is still very early.

pulse.gain: +6.2K stars in its first 9 days. Part of the ArtCraft suite.

steps: [Download FilmCraft](https://github.com/storytold/filmcraft/releases) for your computer (Mac, Windows or Linux) and install it.
Import a video file and try the basics: cut it on the [timeline](https://github.com/storytold/filmcraft#editing) with ripple edit, add a title, and open the color panel to try the color wheels.
Export an H.264 MP4 and check the result. Try the loudness meter to see broadcast-standard audio levels.

footprint.disk: No data found for installer size. Builds from source with `cargo run --release -p filmcraft` (requires Rust 1.95+).
footprint.memory: No data found. Uses a GPU compositor (wgpu) with optional hardware acceleration (VideoToolbox on Mac, Media Foundation on Windows, VA-API or NVENC on Linux).
footprint.runs_on: Mac (universal), Windows (x64, arm64, x86), Linux (x86_64, aarch64), FreeBSD and the web (via WebAssembly).

best_for: You know Premiere's timeline workflow and want a free alternative that speaks the same language - same trims, same shortcuts, same color panel
You need broadcast-standard features (loudness metering, drop-frame timecode, caption formats) in a free editor
skip_if: You need a stable editor for paid work today - FilmCraft estimates itself at 50-60% readiness and its testing on Windows and Linux is limited
You rely on Premiere plugins (VST3, AU, OpenFX) - FilmCraft has no plugin hosting yet

alternatives.name: DaVinci Resolve
alternatives.line: The industry-standard free editor with professional color grading. Far more mature, but proprietary and a much larger install.

alternatives.name: Kdenlive
alternatives.line: A mature free video editor on Linux, Windows and Mac. Stable and well-tested, with a different interface.

watch: **About 50-60% ready for real work.** The project's own estimate. Speed on large footage, plugin hosting and broad camera-file support are the main gaps.
**Part of the ArtCraft suite by storytold.** Same maker as PhotoCraft, LightCraft, PdfCraft and ArtCraft. Early alpha, built by one developer with AI.

**No FFmpeg inside, for better or worse.** FilmCraft implements its own H.264, HEVC, ProRes, VP9 and AV1 codecs. That removes a dependency but means codec support is narrower and less battle-tested than FFmpeg's.
**Windows and Linux get less testing.** The README notes that macOS receives the most testing. Expect more rough edges on other platforms.
